title: The Health Department’s own list, with the reason beside each waiver
question: What reason does the Health Department give when it excuses a nonprofit contract from competition under Administrative Code section 21.42?
finding: The Health Department’s list for fiscal 2024-25 shows 28 contracts excused from competition under section 21.42, with ceilings adding up to $250.7 million. For 23 of them ($239.3 million) the reason written beside the waiver is that the department needs more time to run a competition; 6 of those 23 contracts have terms of five years or more, the longest running from 2018-07-01 to 2027-06-30. The department’s summary for the year puts all its sole-source approvals at $436.4 million.
how: Read from the list the department filed with the Board for fiscal 2024-25 under the Sunshine Ordinance (Administrative Code section 67.24): the table of contracts whose purchasing rule is 21.42, with its "Reason for 21.42" column. Each row’s start date, end date and not-to-exceed amount are as printed; the supplier name is taken from the Supplier Contracts table by contract number. The reasons were sorted into three groups by their wording.
limits: Section 21.42 exists for exactly this: its purpose, in the department’s own words, is to continue services across a gap before a new competition is finished. The question is the length of the gap, not the waiver. One year’s list from one department; the other departments’ lists on disk do not give reasons. The dates are the contract’s whole term, not the length of the waiver, which the list does not state.
